utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd just like to raise one procedural matter before we begin. You'll recall that yesterday, Mr. Karadzic requested time on the basis that he had a number of documents signed by the witness he wanted to show to the witness. After court yesterday, we were able to finish our review of the cross-examination notification and realised there were no documents signed by the witness on that list. We raised this with the Defence team yesterday afternoon, and they informed us they'd make inquiries. We subsequently received, at about 7.00 p.m., a list of six additional documents, and then at 10.00 p.m., a further six documents. Again, none of these 12 documents were signed by the witness. And then this morning, just a minute or so before court commenced, we were handed a list of documents signed by the witness, only one of which is included in English. And obviously this raises concerns for us, as the accused appeared to be aware that he was planning to use these documents at least at some time during the court session yesterday, if not before, and this late notice puts us in a difficult position. And there doesn't seem to be any justification for it in this instance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic or Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do admit, indeed, that due to the rhythm that we have, we have disrupted the order of the steps taken. But please do understand us. This is too important a witness. The rhythm of witnesses is such that we have two witnesses a day, and in view of our resources, that is quite a lot. But, anyway, there seems to have been something wrong in our order of steps. Maybe Mr. Robinson would like to add something to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the first thing I should offer is an apology to the Prosecution for not providing these documents, because it should have been done. And I don't think -- it is a fast pace, and we're buried with new disclosure. But, nevertheless, that's a step that should have been taken, and I apologise on behalf of our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it that you mean to make vigorous effort to comply with the disclosure practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, as much as humanly possible. And we'll consider this the Prosecution's first motion for disclosure violation. They're 51 behind us. But we do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I thought Dr. Karadzic might have raised that himself, but he was far too polite to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll proceed. Thank you, Ms. Gustafson, for your information. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once again, I kindly ask for your understanding and I apologise, General. I'm going to go through a number of documents very quickly. It will be sufficient for you to identify them as your own. 1D3729, please. It seems not to be in e-court yet. Could I please ask the Usher to place this on the ELMO. While we're waiting: General, where were you from August until -- I mean from August 1993 until January 1994? Were you in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Sarajevo. But in the meantime, I was out in the field for a while in the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember this document? You confirmed this yesterday, but I would like the Trial Chamber and the other participants to have this. What you stated here are where the positions -- or, rather, where the commands are, and you say that units want to have submitted -- could you -- is this a document of yours, providing information about where the corps and brigade commands are?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this signature yours, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you bring this document with you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be marked for identification, pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1385, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3721, could we have that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, General, that Mr. Izetbegovic, on the 4th of April, in the evening, declared a general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and the reserve police, or, rather, those forces that he could issue orders to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, but I cannot recall the exact date. Well, that's it, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 5th of April, General Kukanjac responded. Do you agree that this is an order for general mobilisation of all wartime units from the 2nd Military District? And it says here that they should be manned, and if some do not respond to the call-up, that others should be called up straight away. He also says that the courier system should be used; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I looked at this document on several occasions. I had an opportunity to see it earlier on. But I personally heard -- that is to say, I heard myself that when this mobilisation takes place, it is going to be the mobilisation of the Serb people. I heard that from Colonel Gagovic, I heard that in the command of my 216th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this the stamp of the 2nd Military District, and is this the signature of General Kukanjac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, General, did you know that as for this mobilisation of the 4th of April, the Serbs would not respond, and that Mr. Koljevic and Professor Plavsic voted against it and asked people not to be mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that, and I think it's a good thing if that was so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Obviously, there's no translation of this at this point, but I'd just like to add that at line 17, Mr. Karadzic's statement that on the th of April, General Kukanjac responded appears to be just comment by Mr. Karadzic, rather than a reflection of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That is noted. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1386, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, could I ask you to look at 1D3724. It's possible that you may have written it in your own hand. 24, 3724. Do you remember this document? Is this your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the document yet. You'll have to wait a bit. Yes, this is my signature, and this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this say that you are postponing the sending of units from the area of the 1st Corps to the region of Bradina for the next 48 hours, and that the Command of the 6th Corps is going to inform the Main Staff and the 1st Corps when conditions are created for taking in this unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I wrote this personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Chamber how units from Sarajevo, from the city, arrived in Bradina, and can you tell them where Bradina is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bradina is on the road between Sarajevo and Konjic; that is to say, north of Konjic about 10 kilometres. The units from the 1st Corps that went to these areas went via Mount Igman, Pazaric, the Ivan Sedlo Pass, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is how they got out of the city. First across the runway and then through the tunnel; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not leave through the runway because this is the 30th of November, 1993, when the tunnel was open. If they did leave, they went from the area of responsibility of the 104th Brigade from Hrasnica or some other units of the 1st Corps outside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When the tunnel was open, did the units take turns? Did they leave Sarajevo from each brigade, say one battalion went, or another unit, to the zone of the 14th and 16th Division? Previously, it was the operational groups. That was regularly, on a one-month basis that these unit left town and stayed out of town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did stay there, but there wasn't a system involving that it was every month, every 10 days or every 15 days. The units went when necessary and according to developments on the ground. If the situation required that, then sometimes several units went. If not, then units did not even leave Sarajevo. So that was the practice after the tunnel was opened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1387, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3731. [In English] There is translations, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature, and is this a certificate stating that in the family house of Mehmedalija Ramic, in Laticka 30, in the time between the 28th of July up until the 15th of October, 1992, the Command of the 1st Sandzak was stationed there and its command post was there as well. Is something missing here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I was just going to ask if the English could be put at the same time on the ELMO so that others could follow, because this one actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we give the B/C/S version to the witness and put the English translation on the ELMO. I take it the accused has a B/C/S version on his own. Yes. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this command, indeed, in this private house in Stup, so was this true, and was this house mobilised according to the Law on national defence, All People's Defence, where by state organs have the right to use privately-owned and socially-owned property, enterprises, private homes, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document. It's not my signature. Somebody signed on my behalf. To tell you the truth, there were private houses that were used by the soldiers, in practice, but I don't know where this house is and I don't know what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Put the original on the ELMO again. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says here "For Asim Dzambasovic," you're right. Who was this? Can you recognise the signature? It must be a co-worker of yours.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's my operations officer; I think. I'm not sure now. Because I think he is also from Sandzak, Sabro Haskovic. I don't know whether this is his signature. I don't know who it is, but it is one of my associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The number and the date are all in good order; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you the following: According to the Law on All People's Defence, did the state have the right to mobilise property for defence purposes by issuing such orders, such certificates as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state had the right to mobilise them if they weren't being used.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1388, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that they had the right to mobilise privately-owned and state-owned property if it was not being used; houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. If a company has certain buildings and is not using them at that moment, then that area could have been mobilised. Or if a private individual, for any reason, was absent and was not using his or her own home, that could be mobilised as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D3732 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Remember that they sent to the zone of the Joint Command of Konjic, I mean, to reorganise this operations group, or whatever it was; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my first task in the then Republican Staff of the TO, so I was given the task to work in Konjic on the organisation of the Territorial Defence. So it was my first task in the area of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was already the beginning of May 1992; right? That's when the Joint Commission was set up, and you were sent there to put things in order. It says here "Asim Dzambasovic."

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a joint command, actually. I formed a joint command of the TO and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to ask you the following: Do you know about this diagram? Did you create it, was it created on the basis of your orders, or does it show the usual relationship between military commands and civilian authorities; the Presidency of the BiH, and on the one side there is the Main Staff of the TO, and on the other, the Republican MUP, and then further down the War Presidency, and so on? Is this the usual schematic on the basis of the Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not draft this schematic. It was done by someone from the TO Konjic. I personally think that this was done in the case against Zejnil Delalic here. I feel as if I had an opportunity to see it, but this is not my diagram. They refer to my name here, saying that I participated in this, and I can tell by that, too, that I did not draft this schematic. But I didn't draft it, anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we see the general's name in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Mr. Karadzic, when you read out something, please slow down. And I ask you, General Dzambasovic, to put a pause before you start answering the question, for the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you. Let us proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "The Joint Command was the result of the agreement reached between the municipal leadership and the leadership of the Municipal Staff of the TO and the HVO." In your response, it was not recorded in the transcript that this was the Joint Command of the TO and the HVO Konjic. And it says further on: "The co-ordinator from the Republican Staff of the TO of the BiH, Asim Dzambasovic, insisted on that." And so on and so forth. Is this a usual type of schematic? Is this the way things were established in Konjic and also in other municipalities, more or less?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as communications are concerned, or, rather, their chain of command, it is customary in the TO. As for the HVO chain, it's probably the case as well, but I'm not aware of all the details.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted, or, rather, marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to the admission of this document on two bases. First, it appears to be irrelevant, as it relates to the command structure of a location in Central Bosnia that has nothing to do with this case. And, secondly, as far as I've been able to gather in the last five minutes, it comes from a book, it's a page out of a book. It's not a contemporaneous document. And as the witness's answers make clear, he's not really able to confirm much, if any, of the contents of the document, so its reliability is also questionable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness confirmed that this is a customary schematic. What I'm interested in here is the following, and I believe that it will be useful for the Trial Chamber, is the links between the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the War Presidency of the municipality, the MUP, the Territorial Defence, and so on. It is clear that General Dzambasovic - I believe that he was a colonel at the time, or lieutenant-colonel - was sent there to get things in order. That was his primary task. And if he did not draw the schematic himself, this schematic instructor was derived from his work in the field. That is the reason. I haven't read the entire book, but this schematic or diagram can be a document in its own right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm still struggling to understand the relevance of this document, and we are not sure about the provenance of this document. Until then, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1389, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3722, can we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this also your document, in which you ask that they inform you about the decision on grouping units on the Igman front-line? Can you tell us, briefly, what it was that you asked for here?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my document that I signed as the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he answer as to the question what it was about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you tell us, briefly, about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are asking our units at Igman to provide us with information about the area of responsibility of each of the tactical groups and their tasks, about the names of the units in the AOR, from the lowest-ranking up to the level of the brigade, and, finally, the lines of defence. This "P/K" means "Forward End," it's an abbreviation. And also the facilities where those units are located. And then there is a remark at the end stating that this information is essential in order to be able to maintain the working map and to follow the situation in the field. That is the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is this close to Sarajevo, on Mount Igman, above Hrasnica? Is that the army -- is that where the army is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is south of Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I was just going to ask for -- I mean, I can't read the document, but I was just going to ask for more clarity in the question. I don't understand what he meant by "is this close to Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the witness understood. Could you answer the question, and we'll see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that I was supposed to confirm or not whether the units in the area were south of Sarajevo, at Hrasnica, on a plateau of Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they are part of the 1st Corps of the Pazaric Tactical Group which was later the 14th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These names changed, depending on the period, depending on the organisation and reorganisations that were conducted during 1992-1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be tendered, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be marked for identification as Exhibit D1390.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D3730 now on the screen, please. There is a translation. Perhaps we can just look at the signature first, and then the original can be given to the general, and the translation can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your order of the 2nd of January, 1993, where you say that: "The Stup Tactical Group will provisionally organise the defence of the following axes: Main forces, Valter Peric - Petlja-Cenex, and in the auxiliary forces axis along Laticka Street Monastery." Is this all urban combat? Is this all in the city?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and this "G/S," that means the main force would be organising the defence along the axis, and they are stated. And then "PS" is "pomocne snage," auxiliary forces, along the Laticka Street, Monastery Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now it says here what should be defended from Nedzarici and Kasindolska Street, and losses should be inflicted and conditions created to carry out broader offensive combat operations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is normal military operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, could you tell us, please, what was the military objective in the Sarajevo AOR?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The priority military objective was defence, and then to create conditions in any way, along any axis out of the encirclement to break through, to break out of the siege -- out of the besieged town. But these were a little bit unrealistic, these wishes, because in order to do it -- and this is the most difficult action in military tactics, to break out of an encirclement, out of a siege. In order to do that, you had to secure a ratio of forces, according to some theoreticians, a ratio of forces and equipment 7:1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us what was the military objective in the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Before that, while the transcript shows the page: In your previous question, did you not refer to urban fighting or something to that effect? I don't think that's reflected in the transcript. Could you check it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I was asking that the first item in the order, the deployment of the forces in the streets, whether that was preparation for urban combat, and even the streets were mentioned. And the witness confirmed that, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this area is part of the city of Sarajevo, the southern section of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was the military objective of the political leadership of Bosnia and Herzegovina in relation to the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not to upset those from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is something that is known to everyone. The goal of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to defend the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to liberate territories under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. This is clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General, and it's a military goal. I would like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No objection. It appears to be simply comment by Mr. Karadzic on that at line 21 and 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1391, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3723, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous was Exhibit D1391.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this report about the situation on the front in Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 19th of September, 1993? And we will see later that that was your signature?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, probably. I haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can see here in the area of the 1st Corps, assault defence, intense traffic on the route of Pale-Vogosca-Vojkovici-Kasindol-Vraca. These are all areas in Sarajevo; is that right? Relief of units at Igman.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Sarajevo: We have suburban areas of Sarajevo, Vojkovici, Kasindol, Lukavica. Vraca is a part of the central area of town. Rajlovac and Reljevo are suburban neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these neighbourhoods under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska, and are they inhabited, as a rule, by Serbs, majority population?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pale has a majority Serb population. Vogosca was a neighbourhood with a Muslim majority population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can I just ask you this: Did the side in Vogosca control the Serbian side of Vogosca, and the Muslim side controlled the Muslim part of Vogosca, such as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not manage to hear all of the names of the areas in Vogosca that the accused mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, General. The interpreters couldn't hear them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Vogosca, the Muslims controlled mostly the Muslim areas and Serbs controlled mainly the Serb areas, and, for example, Ugorsko as a Muslim settlement, was under the control of the Muslims; that Gornji and Donji Hotonj was under the control of the Muslims, that Kobilja Glava, all of these are parts of the Vogosca municipality, but with a strong concentration of the Muslim population and was this not controlled by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part. It was more or less like that, practically, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can I just summarise? Is it correct that Vojkovici, Kasindol, Lukavica, Vraca, Rajlovac and Reljevo were practically 100 per cent Serb?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it was 100 per cent. All the locations that you referred to are ones with a majority Serb population, except Vraca, where I really don't know what the ratio was. I think there were both Serbs and Muslims there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then here you summarise the situation in other areas; 2nd, 3rd, 4th Corps. Could we look at the last page, please. [In English] Could we get the last page, the next page, please. [Interpretation] Is this your signature and stamp of the Main Staff of the Command?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, this was sent to the president of the Presidency, the vice-president -- the deputy prime minister, the Ministry of Defence, and the deputy commander, Mr. Siber, and the archives. How did your service draft a report like this, let's say this report; on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like any other military personnel, this type of report was drafted on the basis of reports from our subordinate commands and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the reports were sent up from companies, battalions, to brigades, the brigades to corps, and the corps then sent reports to you, if I'm not mistaken, to the Staff of the Supreme Command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in order to make it easier to understand, reporting proceeds up the chain from the lowest-ranking to the highest-ranking unit. Command or ordering proceeds the opposite way from the top-ranking bodies to the lowest-ranking units.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand this will be MFI'd, pending translation. If we could just also reserve any other observations that we might have, as this is a lengthy document and we're not able to comprehend the contents at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1392, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D01207. I think this is in e-court. There is a number. Just a little bit of patience. Perhaps it would be better, while the Usher is still close to the ELMO, to look at the documents that we can still look at on the ELMO. 1D3728, please, can we have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this something that you drafted, the list of the Command for Operative Affairs? You are the chief of that command, and this is your document. Can we now look at 1D3725 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note the previous document was the list was the members of the OP Administration on the 9th of September 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We didn't hear an answer from the witness. Did you answer the question, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did answer, yes. This is the list of my administration at the Kakanj Command Post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the Administration for operations Planning, at whose head you were?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it worked and serviced the whole of the B and H Army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the administrations of the General Staff. And, of course, our activities covered all the units subordinated to the General Staff of the B and H Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3725, please. [In English] 3725.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a request of yours to have information provided to you about an analysis of sabotage operations by Spahica Farm and Jusic base? Since you were not satisfied, you thought that these operations were not successful; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, that I'm asking for an analysis of these operations. That is to say, I am addressing the Command of the 1st Corps with a request for them to carry out a detailed analysis and to explain the actual situation to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, it says that you have some information that they were not exactly successful because of poor organisation of the co-ordination involved?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here. I cannot recall now, but that is what is written in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is Spahica Farm and Jusic base?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth now, I really don't know where these farms are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that is somewhere in Serb territory, because the 1st Corps did not fight with the HVO, or if so, rarely?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is somewhere in the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps. Specifically where this farm is, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we object to this. It's difficult for us -- obviously, we can't read it, but based on the questions and answers, it appears to be irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is relevant. If sabotage operations are underway in the rear, in the depth of the territory, it is legitimate, but it is relevant, and it shows that the side on whose territory sabotage operations are carried out should be cautious. It's the same race, the same language, not to say the same people. That's what we are, and that does justify different kinds of checks and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have to agree, but that's the logic on both sides. If such operations are carried out, it is absolutely soldierly and tactically right to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1394, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3726, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your telegram of the 30th of April, 1995, sent to Avdo Palic in Zepa, in which you are informing him that he has been allowed to transport the persons from numbers 1 through 12, and you also say the daughter of Jusuf Jusupovic, Heneda: "Do inform Jusuf." Is this your communication with your boss?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any communication with Zepa for a while, and I believe, and I believe that this is a telegram of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the same Jusuf Jusupovic who was pro-JNA, pro-Yugoslav-oriented, the one who had to be protected?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, he lost his life in a strange way as he was working on an improvised hydroelectric power-plant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of transportation this is about? That 13 persons would be transported from Zepa; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were wounded persons. They were transported by helicopter, and I think that the UNPROFOR Command was involved in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the usual way to do things? When coming to Zepa, you land on Sokolac territory, and then the examination takes place at Sokolac, and then you proceed; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I travelled to Zepa nine times that way as the head of the team for establishing a protected area, from May 1993 until September 1993. Now, in this particular case, I don't know whether that's the way things actually happened. I cannot say that for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While the witness confirmed that this is his telegram, I'm still struggling to understand the relevance of this document. Could you tell us how this is relevant?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe, Excellency, that one can see here that evacuation is possible and that there is a channel for the evacuation of the wounded from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think Zepa is included in your indictment at all. Is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zepa -- could Mr. Robinson please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I believe certainly the events of Zepa have been the subject of testimony already in the case by David Harland and anticipated to be the subject of other testimony when we deal with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question is whether it's included in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not positive if it's in the indictment, but I believe it's Mr. Tieger who is best placed to answer that question. But the relevance of events in Zepa, I think, have already been established by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1395, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your time is almost up, but how many more documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are some very important documents, Excellency, that are very important for you to have an overview of the situation. Could I please have at least up until the end of this session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should have started with the important ones. You'll have 15 minutes to conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'm going to ask for in-court numbers to place on the ELMO an intercept of yours, a conversation with Fikret Prevljak. Could you identify it briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Our service intercepted a conversation of yours with Prevljak in which you are advocating the release -- or, rather, you're saying that the wounded should be allowed to pass that way. Prevljak is opposing that, and he's also opposing the passage of an UNPROFOR convoy that had not been announced and that has an extra vehicle, at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When you note the trial attorney on the other side rising --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Karadzic didn't provide an identification number, but I don't believe we were notified of this document. This is new to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the explanation is the same, and the apology is the same. We have been burdened with piles of new material, and also the rhythm at which witnesses are being called is very rapid for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why was it not disclosed at the time the other material were handed over to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An oversight, Excellency, a pure oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that you asked Prevljak, Fikret Prevljak, who commanded the unit in Hrasnica, to allow an unannounced convoy to pass that way, and that he should at least allow the wounded to get through? Do you remember this conversation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, among other things, work on such activities as well. I had official contacts with the representatives of international organisations, as the chief of staff and later on the chief of administration. I do not remember this conversation, specifically, but I did carry out such activities; not only in this case, but also in all other cases when it was necessary to negotiate with the representatives of international organisations, regardless of whether it was a question of convoys or requests for electricity, water, or any other humanitarian activity.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we just have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in another thing. In a very soldierly manner, you asked here that civilians be allowed to pass through, and the wounded as well, whereas Fikret Prevljak was opposed to having this unannounced convoy allowed to pass through, and this convoy had an extra vehicle at that. Was this the way things were handled usually, that a convoy had to be announced, and if it was not announced, it would have trouble getting through?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer the question, General: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know where we are in the document, but I saw a page that had different conversations that didn't contain include this witness. If we could clarify where we are at in this document and who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All I know is the conversation between Fikret Prevljak and the witness, and I have no idea. But I understood that the general was able to observe the relevant part of that intercept. Could you help us in that regard, General Dzambasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I did carry out such conversations, and similar ones, but I do not remember this specific conversation because there were many such conversations. The usual practice was that convoys of all kinds be announced, as well as the route that they would be taking, so that through our chain of command, we would ensure conditions for their unhindered passage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If the Chamber is satisfied, may I ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to interpret. Slavuj is answering, and you say, Yes, Slavuj. And he is protesting, saying that a convoy showed up, and no one told him anything. And then he says they have wounded here, and Dzambasovic says, that's the highlighted bit: "Let the wounded pass through." And then he says there are about 10 or 12 vehicles, and they haven't heard of this trouble. And can we have the next page now, please. Do you remember this? Do you remember that there were such cases?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, we did have cases when commanders at local level would not react always, as we had requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see the highlighted bit here? You say: "15, I think." And he says: "You have to know, I am getting the last vehicle out if it is not announced." Is that what soldiers usually did at check-points, that the number of vehicles had to correspond to the number referred to in the announcement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure now whether the number of vehicles had to tally, I mean, the registration plates with the number in the column, itself. However, it is certain that convoys were announced, that's for sure. There was a lot of that. I cannot recall all details.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Two questions. How is this relevant to your case, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it happened on our side, too, that a soldier would not allow 11 vehicles to pass if 10 were announced, or they would not let a convoy through if it had not been announced. So this was practiced throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina on all sides, because a soldierly mind is not creative. They need to have a piece of paper allowing them to let someone get through. The question of convoys is a major issue in my indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So is it the defence, according to your theory, that the other party did the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can answer that. I think what Dr. Karadzic is trying to show is that it was reasonable for the Bosnian Serbs to sometimes refuse to allow convoys to pass when they didn't meet the requirements that had been announced in advance. And in order to show that that is reasonable, he's showing that that practice was also engaged in by the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of the practice that other parties were performing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my second question is: You have no doubt as to the authenticity and legality of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, from our point of view, I couldn't say that we have no doubt. But since the witness has given enough information as to the fact that he at least recalls some of these events, then I think that there's enough evidence to at least mark it for identification. It's part of our practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember you rose, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd just like to note that this document seems to contain multiple conversations. So in addition to the fact that we would have to review it, its admission should be restricted to the conversation discussed in the evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of course, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that this hasn't been interpreted, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1396, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two last topics, General. You agreed with us, during our interview, that there was a practice of placing mobile mortars on a vehicle, mounting them on a vehicle, and then opening fire, and changing positions so that the response fire would not damage the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not agree with you on that question, but I said that by establishment, in the Armija we did not have vehicles that would be used for that purpose. However, in a number of cases, practically, this did happen, and this was mostly done in the unit of the 10th Mountain Brigade, Caco's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more before the final topic. You also agreed that ammunition and weapons supplies did manage to reach Zepa, because -- we're not going to be talking about Srebrenica, because Zepa was in the area of 1st Corps of the B and H Army. I'm not going to show the document, because we don't have time. Do you recall agreeing that this was the practice and that it was successful?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did confirm that to you, with the explanation that when we began to receive reports from Zepa that representatives of the Ukrainian Battalion were leaving check-points under pressure of the Army of Republika Srpska, that they were feeling threatened and that they were asking us, as the superior command, what to do and how they could be helped. After that, at the level of the General Staff, a decision was made to try to provide supplies to Zepa by air, and this was done a number of times.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can you put this -- I would like this to be put on the ELMO, and can we have the in-court numbers for this topic that's important that relates to the incident at the 1st of June, 1993, in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a document of the National Security of the Republika Srpska? Can you please look at it? It is informing that something happened in Dobrinja and that its unit was carried out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to have the reference, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did you refer to an e-court number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In court."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could assist, I think this is Exhibit D341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Why don't we up-load it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that Srdjan Sehovac is reporting here that he has received relating to today's events in Dobrinja, and says that a commander took out his unit to the Dobrinja 3 parking, that they were playing football, and that during the football game, two shells fell, resulting in people getting killed and wounded? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about the incident. I'm seeing the document for the first time, however. It's clear to me that this did happen in Dobrinja. I'm sure that it did happen. As for the details about the wounded, those killed, are something that I don't know. I know that there were quite a few, and I know that as the superior command, we criticised assembling of that type, that it wasn't reasonable at that time to organise sports activities. I am not sure if this was attended just by soldiers. I think that this was a sports event between soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at a document by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the 2nd of June on the ELMO, asking the Supreme Command Staff to prepare a report on this soccer match. I don't know if this was admitted or not. Possibly, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the interview, you told us that you remember that an investigation was launched?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this should be your last question. Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this document and the previous document, D341, were also not notified to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this document in evidence already? I doubt it. No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, I just -- Excellencies, I just have two documents on the same topic, showing exactly who was there, so I would like to ask for your patience and just to ask the general to speak on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After this, I will consult my colleagues whether or not I'll give you extra time. Proceed with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the chief of the Main Staff, Sefer Halilovic, is being informed by the general secretary that the Presidency is asking the Supreme Command to prepare a report on the organising of a football-match on the occasion of the religious holiday of Bajram at Dobrinja, where a large number of persons were killed because of the shelling by the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is what the document says. I'm seeing the document for the first time, however.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could just inform the Court that this document is in e-court at 1D00378.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With English translation. That will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On a very exceptional basis, we allow you to proceed with your remaining two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can we put this on so that we can see what General Fikret Muslimovic responded on the 6th of June. I don't know if he was a general at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it not state here that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see the first page first. Yes, very well. Next page. Yes. Proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it not state here at the top that there was a group of fighters of the 1st Battalion -- of the 1st Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade at Dobrinja, organised thus by a football tournament began at the parking behind the building? Does it not state here that the 1st Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade organised this football-match?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document does confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the bottom, it says, in the second: "Although at an oral briefing that morning, the fighters were warned not to play any matches because of possible shelling, the warnings did not give any results, to which the data on casualties attests, amounting to 58, 11 section commanders, 2 platoon commanders, 1 deputy company commander, 3 orderlies, 4 senior officers from the company." Does this - two couriers and 37 fighters - does this not speak of the number of those who were killed or wounded in that particular incident?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it states in the document. The data that is cited indicates the profile of those who were killed and wounded, and I am seeing this document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the third paragraph, it says that suspicious persons were detained and mistreated, allegedly suspicious persons and fighters, exclusively members of the Serbian ethnicity, which was stopped upon the intervention of the security organs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is also something that is also said in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the document be marked for identification, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see what happened on the 9th of June, what the new information is about that football-match, also coming from General Muslimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, these documents have not been notified to us, and Mr. Karadzic continues to pass over documents and then apologise. But if he has had these documents at least since this morning, at the very least we should have received an e-mail that there were even more documents that he intended to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I hope this is the last document for today and he now understands the problem with disclosure now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, yes, and we have been showing, in the past, and will continue, in the future, to show flexibility.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat what he said in the English because we were overlapping. He spoke before the translation into English was complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say something in English which was not noted?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted the Usher to show the first page, the bottom of the page, for the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 9th of June; is that correct? Do you agree that this contains new information about the football-match on the 6th of June at the improvised pitch, indicating that 12 people lost their lives and 101 persons were wounded, and it speaks about the civilians and fighters who, for several months, have regularly been organising football and other sports activities in this area; the organising for this event was done by -- and the name is mentioned. They're all members of the 1st Battalion. There was a poster on the tournament. And then it states: "Since the majority of the participants of the tournament are members of this battalion, the preparations had been carried out for such a long time, so we can say, with good grounds, that the company commands in this area were informed about the organisation of the tournament."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the rest of his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat from "the organisation of the tournament"? Company commands were informed about this organisation, and then the interpreter couldn't follow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the report here states that the organisation of the tournament began about five or six days before Bajram, and that for several months such football-matches were held on a regular basis, that it was organised by members of the 1st Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade, and their names are stated here, and then a bit lower it says: "In view that the majority of the participants of this tournament were members of the battalion, and since the preparations had been carried out for a long time, it can be stated, on good grounds, that the commands of companies in this area were informed with the organisation of the tournament. This is also confirmed by information that, among the 58 casualties, were 21 commanding officers in the company or the platoon; Omer Oglecevac, deputy commander of one company, was the captain of one of the 14 teams that were registered to participate." So is this a report by General Muslimovic indicating that the organisation took quite some time to carry out and that it was carried out by members of the 1st Battalion of the 5th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We just heard the interpretation of Mr. Karadzic's question. Did you answer the question, General? If you could repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because I was waiting for the end of the interpretation. Everything that you said is stated in the document. I'm seeing this document for the first time, and I am reading the information here for the first time. And as you can see, this is something that is in the jurisdiction of the security organs. This is in their remit, and this is something that was part of their duties. We were just informed about the events, and I know that the event did happen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we admit this? And it's a pity about another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your deputy, Jovan Divjak, submitted his resignation because he felt there was a discriminatory attitude about him? Just like you felt the distrust in Han Pijesak, in the same way, he felt a distrust and was submitting his resignation? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him submitting his resignation, specifically, but we did speak about these things, just the two of us, on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was even arrested, wasn't he? He spent three or four months in prison, did he not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll stop here. This will be marked for identification as Exhibit D1399. We'll have your re-examination after the break, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may reply about the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll stop here. We'll continue with your re-examination by the Prosecution at five past 11.00, and you may be excused, General, since there's one matter I'd like to deal with in your absence. See you later. In the meantime, shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for half an hour and resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, I just have five questions for you, and they're each short, so we shouldn't be more than a few minutes. If you could assist me by focusing your answers as precisely as possible on the exact question, I would appreciate that. The first question relates to your testimony yesterday, when you were asked about Rajko Kusic. And you mentioned that he very often appeared as some representative of the SDS, and this is at page 15171 of yesterday's transcript. And you were asked: "Representative of the SDS or the representative of the local authorities?" And you said: "Well, probably it is the local authorities from the area that he came from." And I'd just like to clarify that answer with you. Was Rajko Kusic an SDS member?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that he was a representative of the local authorities, I meant the area of the municipality of Rogatica. It was the SDS that was in power in Rogatica, as far as the Serb people were concerned. So he's a member of the SDS and he's a representative of the authorities from the municipality of Rogatica. Which specific office he held, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And also yesterday, in relation to your position as chief of staff in the 1st Corps, you were asked about the manpower of the corps, and you affirmed that it was roughly 60.000 soldiers. And I have three questions on this topic. The first is: Of that 60.000, how many were actually -- were located outside the encircled city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally think -- well, right now, I don't have the exact figures here, but I think that in the city, itself, there were about 30.000 men, and that many outside the city as well. At that time, Gorazde was within the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps too, so the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the area of Gorazde, was within the 1st Corps. Also, the unit in Zepa at the time was within the 1st Corps. That is the period of 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And of the 30.000 who were inside the city, how many were located at the confrontation lines at any given time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately, it is my estimate right now - again, I cannot give you an exact figure - but I think it is between 4.000 and 5.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And of the 30.000 soldiers located inside the city, how many of them had weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one quarter, roughly, had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could have D1381 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, the map that's about to appear on your screen is an extract from the ABiH map that you marked yesterday, and it was the map where you marked the location of the Military Hospital and of a gun or a cannon. And that's at the far left of this map. Do you remember making those markings yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And before you made these markings, Mr. Karadzic asked you: "General, can you see that above the Military Hospital, we can see a howitzer on the hospital?" And this was at transcript page 15241. And then he asked you to mark -- you said it was a gun or a cannon, and he asked you to mark that with a circle and put the number 2 at the Military Hospital. And I'd just like to clarify. Is this gun that you circled on the Military Hospital, as the question suggested, or was it, in fact, some distance from the Military Hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance in order to clarify this confusion? I said "on Gorica," and Gorica is a hill above the Military Hospital, the hospital being Bolnica. So perhaps the witness can explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. The Military Hospital is about 500 metres away from this hill. This hill is sparsely populated. There are some areas that are not populated at all. So this hill called Gorica, where these artillery pieces were, is about 500 metres away from the hospital, so it is not on the Hospital Bolnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And earlier this morning, at the beginning of the session, you were asked about mobilisation, and you were shown an order by General Kukanjac of a mobilisation in early April. And in answering that question, you mentioned Colonel Gagovic, and I'd just like to ask you: What was Colonel Gagovic's position in the JNA at that time, early April 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Colonel Gagovic was assistant commander of the 4th Corps for logistics, so the number-one man in the corps, as far as logistics security is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And one last question. Today, you were asked about mobile mortars in Sarajevo, and you said, at page 31 of today's transcript: "Practically, this did happen," referring to the existence of these mobile mortars. And my question for you is: How many of these mobile mortars were in operation in Sarajevo at the time you were the 1st Corps commander -- chief of staff? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was one vehicle where the soldiers of Caco's brigade, the 10th Brigade, used the vehicle in that way. Otherwise, that was not the regular practice, the vehicles that were specialised for that kind of use of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to clarify your answer, because I'm not sure you finished it. The last part of your answer was. "... the vehicles that were specialised for that kind of use of weapons." Did you mean to add anything after that or was that the end of your answer?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the army did not have such vehicles that were special-purpose vehicles like that. The army did not have such vehicles specialised for that. Now, as for these vehicles, I don't know whether there were one or two, but I know that it was this one improvised vehicle upon which the 10th Brigade used that weapon in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies your answer. I have no further questions. Thank you very much, Mr. Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. Thank you, General Dzambasovic. That concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench here, I would like to thank you for your coming all the way to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. And I do apologise to the interpreters if I was too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have a good journey, General. This was on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I take it it is you, Mr. Hayden, that will lead the next evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution calls Mr. Hajrudin Karic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting: Mr. Tieger, I was informed there is a further development in relation to Witness Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I think the -- I believe the Chamber and certainly the Defence was notified accordingly last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So there's no need to issue a decision on the outstanding motion to reject the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I take your point. Yes, I think that probably does pre-empt that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karic. Please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Hajrudin Karic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I would ask for 65 ter 90241, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, on the screen in front of you, you will see a statement which is an amalgamation of your evidence you have provided to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2002 and to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992 and 1993. Have you had an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And is that your signature we see on the B/C/S version of the statement, on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, before I ask you to confirm the accuracy of the statement's contents, there is one correction to make. This correction has already been made by hand in the B/C/S version, but is not yet reflected in the English version. On page 3, at paragraph 10 of the English, the surname of Zeljko Klisara should be spelled with an A, and not an O.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were two further corrections made by hand by the witness to the version he signed, but I'm advised that those minor corrections do not affect the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karic, with those corrections in mind, could you confirm today that the statement is accurate, and if you were asked the same questions on the same topics today, you would provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The corrections are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And just to confirm, Mr. Karic, the corrections are correct and the statement is also accurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I tender this statement into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2839, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I will now read a summary of the statement. Prior to the conflict, Mr. Hajrudin Karic lived in Sarajevo and worked for Centrotrans in Pale. On 22nd of May, 1992, Muslims in Pale were fired from their jobs, and Serb forces began arresting non-Serbs. At the end of May 1992, two Serb policemen arrested Mr. Karic in Pale. He was detained at the Pale Sports Centre, along with over 100 other Muslims. Two days after his arrest, he was beaten by a member of the Serbian paramilitary formation, who told Mr. Karic he was being detained because his brother-in-law had participated in nearby fighting. Mr. Karic was detained at Pale until 11 July 1992. During this time, detainees were barely fed, and Mr. Karic lost tens of kilogrammes in body weight. Detainees were routinely taken out and beaten by Serb forces, including by men belonging to units commanded by Rajko Kusic and Srdjan Knezevic. Many times, the detainees never returned to the room and were presumed killed. By the end of Mr. Karic's stay, only 34 detainees remained. On one occasion, Mr. Karic, himself, was called out and severely beaten. The beating only stopped when another soldier came into the room and told the attackers they were beating up the wrong man.
