I couldn't ask, but I concluded where they were going by what he said. In the afternoon, I heard that there was shooting there, some people were killed, some people were arrested, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this statement of 1997 - that is 1D03680 - you say: "On the 22nd of May, 1992, I returned to Pale. And then in Pale, I came to the conclusion that a larger group of armed soldiers was getting ready with two Pragas, one bus. Rade Hrsum drove it. They were to go to Renovica. Among these masses, I noticed Lazar Bojat. When I heard a comment from him that the soldiers were going to Renovica to slaughter some Muslims, and that they would come back soon." You say here that you saw him among these masses in Pale that evening, and a moment ago you said that you heard him say this by the ticket office?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No way. What do you mean, in the evening? It was that morning. There was no evening. It was in the morning, among these masses of people who were there at the ticket office. He was standing there as the driver who would drive those masses. You keep asking about all this silly stuff, and you stick to this and that. All of this is the truth. I've already told you that. There are no lies here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, maybe I misspoke. It says "a larger group of Muslims," actually, and I misread it as meaning "evening."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here it says: "On the 22nd of May, I returned to Pale." Where did you return from?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: From nowhere. I was there at the ticket office. That's where my uncle lived, right by the building there. I mean, what kind of translation is this? What is this? I have no idea. Where could I be returning from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned that you were going to Sokolac to shop for food, did they check your ID?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, at Sokolac, up there at a check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They saw that you were a Muslim. They let you buy food and return to Pale; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, thanks to the driver who was driving, because I was their boss. So he said something to him. I don't know what he said, but he let me go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said you didn't know about the ultimatum in Renovica for weapons to be surrendered. Did you know about this ultimatum or not?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in the Mandic trial in Sarajevo - 1D3682 is the number of the document; in Serbian, it's page 23, and in English, it's 24 - you said that they set out at 6.00 in the morning, and then you say: "Witness Karic: Because there was this ultimatum presented to Renovica that they had to hand over their weapons because Praca had already surrendered and Podgrab, they had surrendered their weapons, and Renovica, not. And one morning, they got up early. It was about 6.00, and they went in the direction of Renovica." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Possibly, but this was talk amongst these masses of people, Lazar Bojat saying this and that. I mean, what? I wasn't interested in that. It's not important at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is important to me.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there was an ultimatum, and that the others had responded, and that the police did not go there, and Renovica had not surrendered its weapons, and the police, therefore, went there; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what Lazar Bojat said, that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 20, you say that all Muslims were dismissed that day in Pale. This is what this paragraph says: "After that, I did not leave my house because they started arresting Muslims and taking them away. On the day of the attack against the village of Renovica, all Muslims who worked in the municipality of Pale were laid off. Miso Danojlovic, who worked in Centrotrans and who was also commander of the reservists in Pale, told me not to come to work anymore." Were the Muslims in Pale dismissed from work?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: As for Centrotrans, yes. These other companies weren't working anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who were these Muslims who were dismissed from Centrotrans?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: The drivers, and I along with them, and the mechanics that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you give us their names?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, all the Muslims who were there: Hasib Halilovic; Sipovic, Aga; Milutovic, Alija -- Malovic, Dzemo; Ljutovic, Alija; Dzemo; Becic, Vahid; Nesevic, Enver; Ferhatovic, Avdo, and so on and so forth, not to enumerate all of them, all the Muslims who were there; drivers, conductors, I along with them, the mechanics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now let us see whether you were dismissed on the 7th or the 9th of April, when Paradzina came and told you to get away until the situation calmed down?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, because he was not in a position to dismiss me. It was not for him to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then when, on the 22nd, after this fighting in Renovica, Miso Danojlovic came to you and said to you that you shouldn't come to work. Did he actually dismiss you officially? Did he give you a document stating that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, but he said, For your own safety, don't come back to work anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I am perplexed, Mr. Karic. You say that you were detained on the 22nd of May. You say that you were called to the police station?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No. It was on the 28th of May. Actually, sorry, the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 30th?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see now what you said here on the 15th of May, 1993. 1D0368. This is what you say: "The same evening --" or, rather, "the 22nd of May" - here you say it's in the evening - "after the operation in Renovica in 1992, two policemen came to my home and said that I had to go to the police station to give some statement. I set out, came to the police station. However, that evening there was no one to hear me out, and one of the policemen said that I would have to spend the night in detention or, rather, at the old cultural centre." Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: All of it was that way, but that's not the date. I don't know about these dates. I mean, really, they're confusing -- you're confusing them all the time; the 22nd, the 23rd, the 25th, the 28th. Now, was it the 28th or the 30th, but I think that the 30th would be the right date. And it wasn't that evening of the 22nd when they were arrested. It was five or six days later, and then they came to get me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did any one of these arrested persons inform on you because of something?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, because Vehbija Karic is my uncle, so it was only because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once again, please, let us speak slower and let us pause between question and answer. So what you stated in 1993, that the same evening after this operation on the 22nd of May, you were summoned to the police station, that you set out, that you arrived at the police station, that is not correct; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, it's the 30th. Or does it really matter, the 25th, the 30th? I mean, what are you asking me all of this for? It was the 25th, the 30th, whatever date. Who can possibly remember after all of these years?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please don't be so angry. I'm not inventing all of this. I'm reading your very own statement that you gave right after all of this happened in 1993.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you keep sticking to all this silly stuff, and you're asking me all of this silly stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Maybe I'm a bit silly, but this lack of clarity bothers me. So you say, I set out and I arrived. So did you arrive at the police station because you were summoned there?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give any statement at the police station?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were never questioned?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see what you said in the Mandic trial. 1D3682, Serbian page 5, English page 5 also. We can start from Serbian page 4, and in English we can keep page 5. The Prosecutor, Krnjic, asked you about the statement you gave on the 8th of February, 2006, and you said it was the 28th of May. Can you remember exactly which date it was? Now, was it April or May? And you say: "I think it was April. I can't really handle these days anymore. On the 22nd. I think it was on the 28th, it was then, I reckon it was then." Prosecutor Krnjic: "Fine. You have told us that these two policemen told you that you had to make a statement." You say: "The 28th of May," and then you repeat, "May, May." And then on page 5 in Serbian, you say, in English, it's also page 5. Did anyone take a statement from you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No one did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the answer you gave here was: "That evening, when they brought me, no one did, but the next day some person did take a statement from me. I can't remember his name anymore. Well, I don't know what it was called. I think it was some kind of interrogator. He worked in Pale then." So you did give a statement the following day to a policeman in Sarajevo, or at least that's what you said during the trial in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember any longer. I cannot say anything. Did that happen, did that not happen, I really cannot say. Maybe it did, maybe I didn't. Now I'm thinking about it, and I really cannot think and cannot remember any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, thank you. When Judge Rodrigues asked you -- is that actually a foreign Judge in the Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, probably. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This same document, Serbian page 31, English 34-35, you answered the following to Judge Rodrigues: "They only asked me, 'Where is your Uncle Vehbija?'"

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "'We'll catch him. He'll get here too.' And then they accused me of something that happened before the war. Delimustafic's father travelled on the bus and forgot his personal ID card there, and I -- or, rather, one of the conductors brought me that personal ID, and I left it in the drawer. And these drawers are in the table, and it was there perhaps three or four years, I mean this personal ID. And then, I mean, when I was discharged of my duties up there and then when I left from there, they found that ID in the desk, and there you go. They were saying that I had co-operated with Delimustafic, and that was the reason to arrest me, and that was the reason ... ," and so on. And Judge Rodrigues says: "All right. This statement, was it taken in written form or not?" And you say: "It was taken. They typed it out on one of those machines, typewriters."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES SAID
utterances.text: "Did you sign it?" And you say: "I believe they didn't give me anything to sign. I can't remember." So was this Delimustafic, Alija Delimustafic, who was the minister of the interior, was it his personal ID that you had in your desk for four years?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, not his personal ID; his father's ID. His father had travelled. He had lost it. They found it. They brought it to me. He never came to pick it up. And this, what you're -- here, this is what he whispered to me as we were standing. So it wasn't any kind of interview. This was just a conversation in passing in this hall where all of us were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they accused you of co-operating with Minister Delimustafic, and that that was the reason why you were detained?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they think perhaps that it was a forged ID that for some reason you had obtained for yourself?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they were thinking. This ID was there and then this little note pad of his. I never even looked at it. At the time, I didn't even know who this Delimustafic was. I was never interested in politics; not to this day, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. You said here that they asked you about Vehbija Karic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who Vehbija Karic is, otherwise, and what he is to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Vehbija Karic is a relative of mine, a close relative. Well, not that close, not exactly my uncle. I don't know how to explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Vehbija Karic was a general and that he was in the JNA all the way up until the 10th of April, approximately, and then he deserted, he left the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: That, I don't know. I know he was an officer in the JNA. And what kind of officer, and when he left, and whatever, I don't know any of that. I hadn't seen him until a year or so ago. I don't really see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did he later become commander of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you ashamed of Vehbija Karic or are you proud of Vehbija Karic? How come you don't know what your uncle did?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I just told you that he wasn't my uncle and he wasn't that close to me. I am not ashamed of him at all. Why would I be ashamed of him? I didn't contact him that much before the war, during the way or after the war. I'm just telling the truth. We are related, but it's not that we are really in touch a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you said, Because Vehbija Karic is my uncle, my uncle, "amidza," and I believe that that is the Turkish word for paternal uncle. Right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what they said to me, actually, and that is what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But let us look at paragraph 23 of your statement. You say: "After the arrest, two days later a member of the Serb paramilitary formation came to the prison and said to me that I was under arrest because my brother-in-law took part in fighting near the village of Bukovica. On that occasion, he beat me and hit me in the head four times." Who was this brother-in-law of yours?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Zecan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is his last name?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Salispahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his first name?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is his name Ibro Salispahic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it is. Well, it's a good thing you just reminded me. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 1D3719.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a letter of Biljana Plavsic, a member of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency, later vice-president of Republika Srpska. Can we please look at the second page. Those who read English can see that this is information about the aggression of Croatia against the Republic of Srpska, genocide against the Serbs, and so on and so forth. Can we look at page 17 now, please. Do you know where the village of Vukasinovic is? Probably, it's the following page. The paper number is 17, but the e-court page is probably 18. Mr. Karic, do you know where the village of Vukasinovic is?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know that Vukasinovic is between Renovica and Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read to you what happened in Vukasinovici on the 25th of May in English, and then they will translate that for you: [In English] "Village of Vukasinovici, municipality of Gorazde, May the 25th of 1992: A Muslim unit of TD of BH," "TO," probably, "under the command of Suad Hamzic, slaughtered eight Serbs; Veljko Vukasinovic (72); Danica Vukasinovic - Veljko's wife (65), Milos Vukasinovic (64); Jovanka Vukasinovic - Milos's wife (60); Vukasin Vukasinovic (90); Bozana Vukasinovic - Vukasin's wife (75)." Next page, please: "Milorad Vukasinovic (78); and Grozda Vukasinovic - wife of Perko Vukasinovic, the only one who survived the carnage." I don't think Perko Vukasinovic survived; her husband. "After having slaughtered them, the Muslim unit, including Ferid Aganovic and Ibro Salispahic, burnt them down together with their houses. "Next night, the same unit slaughtered nine Serbs in the village of Leleci and burnt down the houses." [Interpretation] Do you know where the village of Leleci is?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I think it's somewhere behind Bare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Objection to this line of questioning. I'm wondering what the relevance is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's going to be very clear, what the relevance is. These are very critical days, and there will be reasons for arrests given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this paragraph, where you were told that you were arrested because your paternal uncle -- or brother-in-law participated in fighting. Actually, not participated in fighting, but slaughtered old men and women in the villages of Vukasinovici and Leleci. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have anything to say. He knows whether this happened or not. It's a matter of whether this is proved or not, but it has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, still, you want to stay away from what he did by forgetting his name; is that the reason why you forgot the name of your wife's brother?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: No, that's not the reason. My wife and I got divorced or separated in 1996. It's been 15 or 16 years since then, and I've forgotten these names.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. It hasn't been authenticated at all by this witness, and in our view, it's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As far as this document is concerned, since the relevant part of the text has been read into the transcript, the Chamber does not find the need to admit this. We'll not admit this, in addition to the reasons referred to by Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you said that in battle, some Muslims in Renovica were arrested and brought to the sports hall in Pale. You stated that in your statement of 1994, 1D3678; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, I didn't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that on that day, the 22nd of May, when they came back, they brought with them captured Muslims from Renovica, they brought them to the Pale Sports Hall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the time, were you hiding in Pale?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd, I was at home. I hadn't gone out anywhere. Had I left the house, perhaps I would have been arrested sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that paragraph, you say: "I was staying and hiding in Pale at my relative's place, and then on the 30th of May, 1992, I was taken to this place in the centre of Pale, where I found approximately 100 others of Muslim ethnicity." And so on and so forth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for you to start hiding on the 22nd of May and not before the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason was that the arrests of Muslims had started. Before that, there were no arrests. There was an attack there on that day, and then they arrested 28 or 30 of them. I think it was 28 or 30, people from Renovica. And then after that, after five or six days later, I was brought, and I joined the other group, and we were all together until the 28th of August, when we were all released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how many Muslims were there in Pale at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, there were as many as were living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it was only you and these hundred people from Renovica that had been arrested. Why weren't all the Muslims in Pale arrested?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, that was your policy, why they weren't arrested. You transferred them all to Sarajevo in buses to get rid of them, to make yourselves look good, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, I'm asking you: Why do you say that you started to hide on the 22nd of May, when the fighting broke out in Renovica, and why were you arrested and not your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, my father-in-law was not arrested because he fled. Also, my mother-in-law, my brothers-in-law, they all left. They managed to escape when the attack was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where were you staying in Pale?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: At my uncle's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He, on the 11th, or on the 9th, or the 10th, or the 11th, they were all transferred to Sarajevo by buses via Hresa. All the refugees from Vrace, Podgrab and Pale were transferred by buses to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which 11th, of what month?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: The month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when wasn't he arrest -- why wasn't he arrested when you were?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, I have no idea why not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say yes to the question whether he was a Muslim? Yes, I now note it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That was my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the statement from 1992 about your detention in Pale, you say, in paragraph 24 -- and you say that in the amalgamated statement, there were about 150 to 200 Muslims in the sports hall. In another statement, you say it was 60. This is in 3625.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, you just keep dwelling on these numbers. I mean, it was a full hall. You weren't allowed -- you didn't dare to speak to anyone or look at anyone. You keep dealing with these things that are unimportant. They were quite irrelevant. Everything that you have been asking me so far has nothing to do with anything. It's all just completely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, all right. Perhaps I'm not much -- a very intelligent person, but there's nothing much that can be done about that. But it is important if we're talking about 60 people, or 150, or 200 people.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: All right, it was a packed hall, as many people as can be fit into a packed hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. And then you say that you were taken out and beaten, and that -- let's find where that is, which paragraph that is. Paragraph 33. They started to curse at you and hit you with a wooden stick on your back, and so on and so forth. Milomir Tepes appeared at the door. And before the examination-in-chief it was written "Tepic," so can we correct that in the transcript, if the witness confirms that it was Milomir Tepes who said, Not him, that's not him."

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you find out who they mixed you up with?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Probably it was the driver, Hasib Halilovic, but I don't know what he could have done wrong. I don't know why they were looking for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know what it is that he did wrong that they wanted to beat him because?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, you didn't have to do anything wrong. They were just looking for anybody just to take it out on them. These were not proper soldiers. These were all civilians, people. Their only fault was that they were Muslims, as far as you're concerned. I'm talking about the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then they stopped hitting you, and they pushed you back into the hall. They stopped when this guy warned them that you were not the one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a statement from 1993 - this is 13677 - you said that there were two dead bodies in the room where you were. And then after that, you never again mentioned those two bodies?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: When somebody would ask me, I would answer. I don't know that I didn't mention them. Every time I spoke about that, these were innocent people who were killed. I knew them from before the war, who they were, what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 36 of this statement, you mention an event relating to Fahrudin Sipovic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Sipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sipovic or Sipovic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Sipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right, Sipovic. So the event is mentioned only in your statement from 1992. This is 65 ter 22134. Why did you never mention that before?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC
utterances.text: Well, I actually did. That was the first statement. It was very important, and these were the people who were killed, beaten the most, who had suffered the most in captivity in this war. There were numerous others, but these are the ones that I remembered and the ones that I knew before we were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what you said in paragraph 36 -- 36, not 65; 36: "On the 6th of July, 1992, I was ordered to go to the --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. I'm trying to keep up with the pace here, but I'm struggling to find the references here, particularly this last one to the 1992 statement. If we could have some direction, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have it on the screen. This is 65 ter 22134, and it's on the screen. The Registrar found it. No, I'm sorry, this is the last statement. Just one moment. This is the statement from 1993. That is 1D3677, and it says: "On one occasion, I was taken to that room. And the room where I was taken to, there were already two dead bodies there who had been killed by sticks, wooden sticks." And this is 1D3677.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the amalgamated statement, paragraph 36, you say: "On the 6th of July 1992, I was ordered to go out to the locker room to get one detainee. My left hand still hurt from the blows. I saw Fahrudin Sipovic on the floor. He couldn't get up. His arm was broken, and he was all bloody. He tried to get up, and then when he almost made it, the soldier again hit him with a piece of wood. I forgot my pain. I helped Fahrudin to stand up and brought him back to the hall. Fahrudin survived the beatings. As far as I know, today he is working as a policeman in Renovica." There is no "two dead bodies" there. In the amalgamated statement, you do not mention these two who are dead, and that is your final statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can we please bring up the statement that apparently contradicts what the witness just said so he can at least see that for himself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do that tomorrow. Mr. Karadzic, you'll have exactly five minutes tomorrow, not a second more. There's one further matter. From tomorrow on, with the agreement of the staff members, we revert to the original sitting schedule, when we are sitting in an extended format, i.e., 9.00 to 3.00, meaning that we'll have an hour break from 12:30 to 1:30. Mr. Karic, we have to adjourn for today. I appreciate your patience. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.32 p.m.,
